scoring_justification: Checker fits functional forms (power law, exponential, stretched exponential) to the raw polarization curves and compares fitted exponents / goodness-of-fit to the theoretical predictions derived from the model parameters (d=3, μ=3). No self-reported metric is trusted.

hidden_assets.purpose: Theoretical exponents for uniaxial slow (power law p=0.5) and fast (stretched exponential β=0.5) regimes, derived from model parameters d=3, μ=3.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Exponent computed as d/(2μ) = 3/(2*3) = 0.5. For multiaxial slow, no target exponent; only exponential goodness-of-fit (R² > 0.9) is required.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are deterministic physical constants directly from the paper's equations; they are not invented but are the exact analytical predictions.

outputs.description: Ensemble-averaged spin polarization curves for three regimes: (A) uniaxial slow (ν/W=1e-3), (B) multiaxial slow (ν/W=1e-3), (C) multiaxial fast (ν/W=10). The checker will fit the functional forms (power law, exponential, stretched exponential) to the tail of the data and compare the extracted exponents to the theoretical predictions.

output_contract.notes: The solving agent must produce this CSV from its own Monte Carlo simulation; no other output is scored. The hidden checker recomputes fitted exponents and compares them to the paper's theoretical values (d/(2μ)=0.5 for the power law and stretched exponential). The agent need not compute the analytical curves explicitly.
